thread:
tanvi: Quick sync — I pushed a short PRD draft for the routing/catalog prioritization problem: https://docs.internal/redwood/routing-catalog-prd (please pretend the link works). TL;DR: customers are hitting inconsistent fallbacks across regions, want clearer priority rules and launch gates. Need ACs + edge cases by EOD.

sasha: skimming now. can we get a one-line definition of "compatibility" vs "preferred_variant"? keeping those separate helps decisions.

tanvi: good call. one-liner: `compatibility = binary runtime/IO compatibility` (model accepts same inputs/outputs), `preferred_variant = cost/latency-preference (non-blocking)`. i'll add to doc.

miguel: infra concerns: if we route by preferred_variant we must ensure we have capacity headroom and a fallback plan that doesn't increase cross-region traffic too much. otherwise egress + latency explode.

kate: also ML note — "compatible" doesn't guarantee semantic parity. fallback should be labeled as "graceful" vs "strict" depending on QA pass on prompt set.

oliver: from solutions/customer POV — two enterprise customers asked for sticky routing to the same variant for regulatory reasons. that's high priority for them but low for self-serve.

sasha: propose prioritization matrix: (1) regulatory stickiness, (2) SLA-bound customers, (3) cost-sensitive defaults, (4) ML-quality fallback. we should map customers to these tiers.

tanvi: adding a draft matrix to the PRD. can we spell out launch acceptance criteria? here's a first pass — please react and refine. :point_down:

sasha: lgtm, but tighten numbers.

miguel: i put inline suggestions.

kate: +1 on tests.

tanvi: [ACs pasted]
```
Acceptance Criteria (draft):
- Routing determinism: 99.9% of identical routing keys resolve to the same variant within a single region over 24h window.
- Fallback latency impact: end-to-end additional p95 latency due to fallback < 30ms for 95% of requests.
- Compatibility contract: fallback allowed only when compatibility matrix shows "IO-compatible" and model tokenization differences flagged.
- Quality safeguard: automated regression check against canonical prompt set — no MORE than 5% drop in pass-rate for critical prompts when fallback exercised.
- Observability: per-route counters, per-variant traces, and an alert when fallback rate > 0.5% over 10m.
- Rollout: canary -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% with rollback automation on alert.
```

sasha: edge cases to add:
- region preference mismatch (user pinned to region A but capacity hit -> should prefer same-region fallback variants only)
- model family incompatibility (eg. llama2 -> gpt-style) -> block fallback
- tokenization drift -> flag and analyze (don't auto-fallback if drift exceeds threshold)

miguel: add capacity gating: if fallback causes cross-region traffic > 5% of total for a route, pause and alert ops.

oliver: customer asks: can we expose a "routing priority" flag in the API so enterprise can opt-in? this will affect rollout/migration.

kate: yes we should have an API flag and a console toggle. include in AC: admin override for enterprise accounts only.

tanvi: decision proposal: scope MVP for Q3 (hosted + dedicated), ship API flag for enterprise, console toggle, observability dashboard, and the canary rollout plan. leave private/VPC advanced rules for Q4.

sasha: sounds reasonable. add acceptance gate: 48h stability on canary for both latency and fallback rates before 10% increase.

miguel: i'll own deployment plan and capacity checks + the cross-region guard rails.

kate: i'll own the compatibility matrix and the regression prompt suite.

oliver: i'll draft customer comms and the opt-in flow.

deploy-bot: plan recorded: routing-catalog-prd v0.2 created by tanvi. canary policy template attached.

tanvi: thanks all — i'll fold these into doc and ping again for final sign-off tomorrow. if anyone has blockers for ownership, call out here. :thumbsup:
